commits.message: The stagger tests say why they may stagger lifecycles (rich-animation-42lg.h4r)

A stagger starts its earliest child at 0, and a lifecycle is staggered by its own entered (rich-animation-42lg.h4r)

Review (high) on #490:
- A negative delay now starts the last child at 0: origins shift by the lowest of them.
- The span (delay times the last index) is refused by the delay's name when it overflows.
- Animation.all folds instead of spreading into Math.min/max, which throws past the engine's argument limit.
- Docs and the timeline header stagger a loop, not lifecycles: a lifecycle's turn is its entered, on the host clock its leave and gone take.
- Tests pin answers exactly (nextDown, now one helper for three suites) instead of against the implementation's own expression.

A stagger runs one animation across children, each offset by its index (rich-animation-42lg.h4r)

Timeline.stagger(animations, delay) is Animation.all of Timeline.run, each
child on a timeline playing from index × delay. The group changes when the
soonest child does, and each child's answer is carried onto the stagger's
clock. Group, Table rows, Tree children and Layout panes take the frames
through Animation.map, and none of them changed.

A Tree child that draws no rows still takes a fork guide. That is filed as
rich-animation-42lg.8qh, and the docs example uses a Group.

A frame says when it changes on the host's clock, stamped in one place (rich-animation-42lg.uv8) (#489)

* A frame says when it changes on the host's clock, stamped in one place (rich-animation-42lg.uv8)

Only a renderable built for the draw site's t stamps (stampFrame: frameAt,
Frames, Spinner.drawnAt, Effected, GlyphEffected). Nothing an animation's at
returns carries a stamp; its change reaches the host through nextChange.
Transition holds one schedule and done is read off it; Animation.onBeat is
the one stepping rule; lifecycle's holds are Timeline.run of the schedules.
A bare-stamp carrier after a line break takes no row; an empty text frame
keeps its stamp.

* A frame of no cells says when it changes on a carrier that opens no row (rich-animation-42lg.uv8 review)

splitLines no longer guesses a carrier from its style: Segment.carrier is a
control of no codes, so a stamp at Infinity, an empty text frame and a
change's line end all keep the rows they have unstamped.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* An element is gone when it stops drawing, and a crop keeps every control (rich-animation-42lg.uv8 review)

gone reads the goneAt phase draws from, so a stepped exit is never asked
about -Infinity before leave. adjustLineLength keeps controls past its cut,
so a carrier after a cropped row still says when its frame changes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* A crop keeps every piece of no cells, and one function makes every stamp (rich-animation-42lg.uv8 review)

adjustLineLength keeps an empty piece at the cut again. frames.ts builds every
stamp style through stamp(). The transitions demo stamps its change through
frameAt, and the docs name the stamping renderables in one place.
